body: For each independent target Pauli and flag site, commutation with J_z kills the flag X/Y coefficients; commutation with J_x then kills the remaining Z coefficient. Linear independence prevents cancellation across sites or target factors. Flag-only Heisenberg exchange is a scalar under collective rotations but does not itself entangle the flag with a target. The singlet-controlled target operator commutes with collective SU2 and is a valid abstract operation, but depends on a flag-pair/target port absent from the original one-spin controls. This is not a no-go for all hardware, effective pulse synthesis or bounded-noise protocols. Two-spin collective-Z protection cannot simply be relabelled as all-axis protection. The source rank27 and128-dimensional simulation figures remain unacquired numerical reports; the stated restriction follows from the displayed analytic coefficient argument.
